lines.text: In 1977, a telescope picked up a signal from space so strong, the astronomer wrote one word next to it.
It hit Ohio State's Big Ear radio telescope on August 15th, 1977.
It lasted 72 seconds, exactly as long as the telescope could watch that spot in the sky.
On the printout it showed up as six characters. Six, E, Q, U, J, five.
Astronomer Jerry Ehman circled them and wrote Wow in the margin.
Astronomers searched that patch of sky again and again. It never came back.
In 2024, researchers suggested a rare flare from a cold hydrogen cloud. It is still not proven.
So was it nature, or someone saying hello?

sources.claim: Detected August 15, 1977 by Ohio State's Big Ear telescope; lasted the full 72-second window; Jerry Ehman wrote Wow!
6EQUJ5 encodes signal intensity, not a message; follow-up searches never detected it again
2024 preprint proposes a cold hydrogen cloud brightened by a stellar flare; not yet confirmed

publish.title: 72 Seconds From Deep Space That Never Came Back 📡
publish.description: In 1977 a radio telescope caught a signal so strong the astronomer wrote "Wow!" next to it. It has never been heard again.
